duas.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
duas.translation: All praise is due to Allah who fed us and gave us drink and made us Muslims.
In the name of Allah and upon the blessing of Allah.
In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ الْمَوْلَجِ وَخَيْرَ الْمَخْرَجِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا
duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You for the good of entering and the good of exiting. In the name of Allah we enter, and in the name of Allah we exit, and in Allah our Lord we trust.
wbw: and in the name of Allah

duas.translation: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبْثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ
duas.translation: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female devils.

duas.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, I have placed my trust in Allah; there is no power and no strength except with Allah.
O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ حَسَّنْتَ خَلْقِي فَحَسِّنْ خُلُقِي
duas.translation: O Allah, just as You have made my external form beautiful, make my character beautiful as well.
May Allah have mercy on you.
wbw: May He have mercy on you

duas.arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ، مَجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا، إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, its course and its mooring. Surely my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.

duas.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
duas.translation: All praise is to Allah who gave us life after having taken it from us, and to Him is the resurrection.

duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ كَسَوْتَنِيهِ، أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِهِ وَخَيْرِ مَا صُنِعَ لَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهِ وَشَرِّ مَا صُنِعَ لَهُ
duas.translation: O Allah, praise be to You. You have clothed me with it. I ask You for the good of it and the good for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of it and the evil for which it was made.

data.verse: Those who restrain anger and pardon people — Allah loves the doers of good.
data.hadith: The strong is not the one who overcomes people by his strength, but the one who controls himself when angry.
data.note: Seek refuge from Shaytan, sit down, and make wudu.

data.verse: Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
data.hadith: Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
data.note: Try reciting Surah Ash-Sharh and take deep breaths.

data.verse: Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
data.hadith: Know that if the entire nation gathered to harm you, they could not harm you except with what Allah has decreed.
data.note: Recite the last two surahs (Al-Falaq, An-Nas) for protection.

data.verse: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.
data.hadith: He who does not thank people does not thank Allah.
data.note: Say 'Alhamdulillah' often today and thank someone around you.

data.verse: Indeed, Allah loves those who turn back to Him in repentance.
data.hadith: All the sons of Adam are sinners, and the best of the sinners are those who repent.
data.note: Make wudu, pray two rak'ahs, and seek forgiveness sincerely.

data.verse: Say: In the bounty of Allah and His mercy — in that let them rejoice.
data.hadith: A cheerful face for your brother is charity.
data.note: Share your happiness — smile, give, and praise Allah.

data.verse: And whoever fears Allah — He will make for him a way out.
data.hadith: How wonderful is the affair of the believer — all of it is good.
data.note: Hold onto good thoughts about Allah — He answers them.

data.verse: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.
data.hadith: Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost camel in the desert.
data.note: The door of tawbah is always open — turn back.

data.verse: And We are closer to him than his jugular vein.
data.hadith: Allah says: I am as my servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.
data.note: You are never alone — dhikr brings the heart company.

data.verse: Whoever puts his trust in Allah — He will be sufficient for him.
data.hadith: If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance He deserves, you would be provided for as the birds are.
data.note: Pray two rak'ahs of Istikhara and trust the outcome.

data.verse: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.
data.hadith: No fatigue, illness, sorrow, sadness, hurt or distress befalls a Muslim — even a thorn — but Allah expiates some of his sins for it.
data.note: Make sincere du'a — sadness is a means of purification.

data.verse: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
data.hadith: Take advantage of five before five: your youth before old age, your health before sickness…
data.note: Rest is worship when it renews your service to Allah.

pillars.name: Shahādah
pillars.source: Narrated by Ibn ʿUmar (RA): The Prophet ﷺ said, "Islam is built upon five: to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to pay zakat, to perform Hajj, and to fast Ramadan." (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16)

sections.heading: The testimony
sections.body: Ash-hadu an lā ilāha illa-Llāh, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasūlu-Llāh — I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

sections.heading: Its meaning
sections.body: It is a rejection of every false object of worship and a sincere affirmation that worship is due to Allah alone, and that Muhammad ﷺ is His final Messenger whose guidance is to be followed.

sections.heading: Its place
sections.body: It is the gateway to Islam: a person enters the faith by sincerely uttering and believing it, and it is the foundation on which the other four pillars stand.

pillars.name: Ṣalāh
pillars.source: Narrated by Ibn ʿUmar (RA): The Prophet ﷺ said, "Islam is built upon five: to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to pay zakat, to perform Hajj, and to fast Ramadan." (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16)

sections.heading: Five daily prayers
sections.body: A Muslim prays five obligatory prayers each day: Fajr, Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ, facing the Kaʿbah in Makkah.

sections.heading: Its importance
sections.body: Salah is the first matter a person will be asked about on the Day of Judgement. It is the direct link between the servant and his Lord, performed in cleanliness and humility.

sections.heading: Beyond ritual
sections.body: Allah says the prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing (Qur'an 29:45) — it is meant to shape character, not only mark the day.

pillars.name: Zakāh
pillars.source: Narrated by Ibn ʿUmar (RA): The Prophet ﷺ said, "Islam is built upon five: to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to pay zakat, to perform Hajj, and to fast Ramadan." (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16)

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Zakat is an obligatory annual charity of 2.5% on wealth held above a minimum threshold (niṣāb) for a lunar year. It is paid to eight categories defined in Surah at-Tawbah (9:60).

sections.heading: Its purpose
sections.body: It purifies wealth and the heart from greed, lifts up the poor and indebted, and binds the community together as one body.

sections.heading: A right, not a favour
sections.body: The Qur'an describes zakat as a right of the needy upon the wealthy (51:19) — not a generous gift, but a due owed to Allah and to His servants.

pillars.name: Ṣawm
pillars.source: Narrated by Ibn ʿUmar (RA): The Prophet ﷺ said, "Islam is built upon five: to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to pay zakat, to perform Hajj, and to fast Ramadan." (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16)

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Every adult, healthy Muslim abstains from food, drink, and intimacy from dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib) during the month of Ramadan.

sections.heading: Its purpose
sections.body: Allah says: 'O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you... that you may attain taqwa' (Qur'an 2:183). It trains the soul in patience, gratitude, and self-restraint.

sections.heading: More than hunger
sections.body: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need that he give up his food and drink (Sahih al-Bukhari 1903).

pillars.name: Ḥajj
pillars.source: Narrated by Ibn ʿUmar (RA): The Prophet ﷺ said, "Islam is built upon five: to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, to pay zakat, to perform Hajj, and to fast Ramadan." (Sahih al-Bukhari 8, Sahih Muslim 16)

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Hajj is the pilgrimage to the sacred House in Makkah, performed in the month of Dhul-Hijjah, obligatory once in a lifetime upon every Muslim who is able physically and financially.

sections.heading: Its rites
sections.body: The pilgrim enters iḥrām, performs ṭawāf around the Kaʿbah, saʿy between Ṣafa and Marwa, stands on the plain of ʿArafah, stones the pillars at Mina, and offers a sacrifice.

sections.heading: Its reward
sections.body: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever performs Hajj for Allah's sake and does not commit obscenity or transgression returns as the day his mother bore him' (Sahih al-Bukhari 1521).

articles.name: Belief in Allah
articles.source: Narrated by ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (RA): Jibrīl (ʿAS) came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked, "Tell me about īmān." He ﷺ said: "It is to believe in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and to believe in the Divine Decree — its good and its evil." (Sahih Muslim 8; the meaning is also in Sahih al-Bukhari 50)

sections.heading: Who he was
sections.body: Adam was the first human and the first Prophet of Allah. He was created by Allah from clay and given life by Allah's command. Allah taught him the names of all things and commanded the angels to prostrate to him as a sign of honour.

sections.heading: In Paradise
sections.body: Adam and his wife Hawwa were placed in Paradise and permitted to enjoy everything in it except one tree. Iblis whispered to them and they ate from the forbidden tree, after which they were sent to Earth as Allah had decreed.

sections.heading: Repentance
sections.body: Adam learned words of repentance from his Lord, turned back to Him, and Allah accepted his repentance — a reminder that the door of tawbah is always open.

sections.heading: Legacy
sections.body: Adam is the father of mankind. His story teaches responsibility, the enmity of Shaytan, and the mercy of Allah.

sections.heading: His knowledge
sections.body: Idris is mentioned in the Qur'an as a man of truth and a Prophet. Scholars say he was among the first to write with the pen and to study the stars.

sections.heading: His rank
sections.body: Allah raised him to a high station, as mentioned in Surah Maryam (19:57).

sections.heading: His call
sections.body: Nuh called his people to worship Allah alone for 950 years, but only a few believed.

sections.heading: The Ark
sections.body: Allah commanded him to build a great Ark. When the flood came, the believers and pairs of every kind were saved while the disbelievers were drowned.

sections.heading: Lesson
sections.body: Patience in da'wah and trust in Allah's plan, no matter how few respond.

sections.heading: His people
sections.body: Hud was sent to the powerful tribe of 'Ad, who built tall monuments and were arrogant due to their strength.

sections.heading: Their end
sections.body: When they rejected him, Allah destroyed them with a furious, sustained wind. Hud and the believers were saved.

sections.heading: The she-camel
sections.body: Salih was sent to Thamud. As a sign, Allah brought forth a she-camel from a rock. The people hamstrung her, defying Allah.

sections.heading: Their punishment
sections.body: They were seized by a mighty blast and destroyed for their arrogance.

sections.heading: Friend of Allah
sections.body: Ibrahim is called Khalil-ullah, the close friend of Allah. He smashed the idols of his people and stood alone for tawhid.

sections.heading: The fire
sections.body: Nimrod threw him into a great fire, but Allah commanded the fire to be cool and safe for him.

sections.heading: Sacrifice
sections.body: He was tested with the command to sacrifice his son Ismail; both submitted, and Allah ransomed Ismail with a great ram.

sections.heading: Legacy
sections.body: He and Ismail built the Ka'bah in Makkah and called people to Hajj.

sections.heading: His people
sections.body: Lut was sent to the people of Sodom who committed great immorality. He warned them but they refused.

sections.heading: Their destruction
sections.body: Their cities were overturned and stones of baked clay rained down upon them; Lut and the believers were saved.

sections.heading: Son of Ibrahim
sections.body: Ismail was the firstborn son of Ibrahim and Hajar. He showed great patience and submission to Allah from a young age.

sections.heading: Zamzam
sections.body: When left in the valley of Makkah, his mother ran between Safa and Marwa, and Allah caused Zamzam to spring forth for him.

sections.heading: The Ka'bah
sections.body: He helped his father Ibrahim raise the foundations of the Ka'bah.

sections.heading: Glad tidings
sections.body: Ishaq was the son of Ibrahim and Sarah, given as glad tidings in their old age.

sections.heading: A prophet from a prophet
sections.body: He was a prophet, and his son Ya'qub continued the prophetic line.

sections.heading: Israel
sections.body: Ya'qub, also called Isra'il, was the son of Ishaq and father of the twelve tribes.

sections.heading: Patience
sections.body: He bore the loss of his beloved son Yusuf with beautiful patience until Allah reunited them.

sections.heading: The dream
sections.body: As a boy, Yusuf saw a dream of eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him — a sign of his future.

sections.heading: Trials
sections.body: He was thrown into a well by his brothers, sold into slavery, tested with temptation, and imprisoned unjustly — yet remained patient and pure.

sections.heading: Reunion
sections.body: Allah raised him to authority in Egypt, where he was reunited with his family and forgave his brothers.

sections.heading: His trial
sections.body: Ayyub was tested with the loss of his wealth, family, and health for many years. He never complained to anyone but Allah.

sections.heading: His relief
sections.body: Allah commanded him to strike the ground with his foot; a cool spring gushed out and restored him completely.

sections.heading: Justice in trade
sections.body: Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan to call them away from cheating in measures and weights.

sections.heading: Their end
sections.body: When they rejected him, an overwhelming blast seized them and they were destroyed.

sections.heading: Early life
sections.body: Musa was raised in the palace of Fir'awn after Allah inspired his mother to place him in the river.

sections.heading: The call
sections.body: Allah spoke to him directly at the blessed valley of Tuwa and sent him to Fir'awn with clear signs.

sections.heading: The exodus
sections.body: He led the Children of Israel out of Egypt; Allah split the sea for them and drowned Fir'awn.

sections.heading: The Torah
sections.body: Allah revealed the Tawrah to him on Mount Tur.

sections.heading: Brother of Musa
sections.body: Harun was the brother of Musa and his vizier, gifted with clear speech.

sections.heading: His role
sections.body: He supported Musa in confronting Fir'awn and guiding the Children of Israel.

sections.heading: Among the patient
sections.body: Allah counts him among the patient and the righteous in the Qur'an. He upheld justice and kept his promises.

sections.heading: King and Prophet
sections.body: Dawud defeated Jalut (Goliath) and Allah gave him kingship, wisdom, and the Zabur.

sections.heading: Worship
sections.body: He was the most devoted in worship — fasting alternate days and standing in prayer at night.

sections.heading: His kingdom
sections.body: Sulayman, the son of Dawud, was given a kingdom unlike any other — control over the wind, jinn, and the speech of animals.

sections.heading: Queen of Sheba
sections.body: He invited the Queen of Sheba (Bilqis) to Islam, and she submitted with him to the Lord of the worlds.

sections.heading: Against Ba'l
sections.body: Ilyas was sent to a people who worshipped an idol called Ba'l. He called them to worship Allah alone.

sections.heading: The chosen
sections.body: Allah counts him among the excellent and the chosen. He continued the work of Ilyas.

sections.heading: The fish
sections.body: Yunus left his people in frustration without permission and was swallowed by a great fish.

sections.heading: His du'a
sections.body: In the darkness he called out: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You; indeed I was of the wrongdoers.' Allah saved him and brought his people to faith.

sections.heading: Du'a for a son
sections.body: In old age Zakariya prayed for a righteous heir, and Allah granted him Yahya as a sign.

sections.heading: Pure youth
sections.body: Yahya was given wisdom while still a child, and was dutiful, pure, and god-fearing.

sections.heading: Miraculous birth
sections.body: Isa was born to Maryam by Allah's word, without a father, as a sign for mankind.

sections.heading: His miracles
sections.body: By Allah's permission he healed the blind and the leper, gave life to the dead, and made a bird from clay.

sections.heading: His message
sections.body: He called Bani Isra'il to worship Allah alone and gave glad tidings of a Messenger to come after him named Ahmad.

sections.heading: His ascension
sections.body: He was not crucified; Allah raised him to Himself, and he will return before the Day of Judgement.

sections.heading: The final Messenger
sections.body: Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the Prophets, sent as a mercy to all the worlds.

sections.heading: Revelation
sections.body: The Qur'an was revealed to him over 23 years through the angel Jibril, beginning in the cave of Hira.

sections.heading: His character
sections.body: His wife Aishah said his character was the Qur'an — truthful, merciful, just, and humble.

sections.heading: His legacy
sections.body: He established the religion, completed the message, and left behind the Book of Allah and his Sunnah as guidance until the Day of Judgement.
